# BOOK 1 NOTES: "Dick Merriwell's Heroic Players; Or, How the Yale Nine Won the Championship" (Burt L. Standish, Street & Smith, 1912; Gutenberg #63608)

Front matter (ads): Merriwell series list (101–221), Alger series, Nick Carter list, Tales of the Rolling Plains (Diamond Dick/Buffalo Bill), Round the World Library (Jack Harkaway). Ignore for story questions.

## Main characters
- **Dick Merriwell**: Yale "universal coach", master of strategy, honest, father-like. Also Dick and Jim have code bird/animal calls. Friends Chester Arlington (engineer, Valdivia) and June (his sister, Dick's love).
- **Jim Phillips**: sophomore Yale pitcher, star, later elected baseball captain. Friends: Bill Brady (catcher, big, deep bass voice; father owns Elm National Bank stock), Harry Maxwell, Sam Taylor (senior catcher), Bob Gray (senior pitcher), Jack Tempest (Virginian sprinter), Woeful Watson (pessimist), Steve Carter (third base), Sherman (captain, first base, senior), Jackson (second base), Winston (substitute pitcher), Hasbrook (New Haven Country Club captain), Caxton, Horton, Reid (Harvard shortstop/batter).
- **Villains**: Parker (junior, big guard, football; Wesley Parker), Carpenter (grind, glasses), Shesgren (sophomore, blue eyes, glasses, thin voice; later turns honest), Paul Foote (undersized, smokes cigarettes, father rowed crew; Foote's father promised Y/trip), Harding (gambler, politically powerful in NY), Barrows (gambler, schemer, "Pete"), Svenson (Norse skipper of yacht Marina), Dennison (weak investor), Barnes (Harding's agent), Bascom (wireless man, electrician, artist with brushes), Marsten ("Johnny", gambling house New Haven, "Bunny"), Riggs (paying teller, Elm National Bank), George Boyd (Ku Klux, maimed right hand), Calhoun (Cal) Conly (Roselands nephew, joined KKK, later repents), Dick and Walter Percival/Conly (Roselands cousins, mischief-makers), Hastings (bank cashier), Bromlow (bank president), Phelps (financier, enemy of Dick's Maine lumber venture), Snell/"Martin" (detective), Dr. Savage (drunk doctor, KKK), Bill Dobbs, Jones (New Haven detective).
- Harvard: Bowen (captain, catcher), Briggs (pitcher), Wooley, Hobson (ex-Harvard star), Farquar, Renshaw, Neilson (Harvard crew coach), Thompson (Harvard coach), Hazlitt.
- Yale crew: Murchison (stroke, captain), Flagg (seat 7), Rogers (cox), Harper (bow). Coaches: Benton, Hargreaves.
- Others: Canfield (professor), Dean, Gordon (instructor), Sam (old rubber), Uncle Joe, Aunt Dicey, Gurney, Danby, Angell, Foote's "Gordon" the instructor.

## Sequence of events
1. Ch I: Jim and Bill practice hitting high balls vs Harvard (Briggs, controls; Bowen catcher). Dick says "inside baseball" matters.
2. Ch II: Gurney bets; Watson's pessimism; Carpenter and Shesgren jealous; Parker overhears, recruits them with plan to "show up" Jim. Parker wants Carter as captain; Tempest insulted by Parker ("I don't remember saying anything to you, Tempest").
3. Ch III: Hasbrook asks Jim to pitch Country Club vs Boston Athletic Assn; Dick consents with conditions. Hobson drafted by Boston. Parker, drinking, with Carpenter/Shesgren on club porch; reveals plan. A stranger receives a letter; Parker tells him "Safe enough."
4. Ch IV: Carpenter and Shesgren call on Jim; Jim says two registered letters; one vanished. Game: Jim and Hobson pitch; Brady homers; Jim strikes out 3 on 9 pitches; Hasbrook wins it on an error (score tied 6–6 then Hasbrook wins). Bowen: "Good work, Phillips!"
5. Ch V: Bowen (Harvard) files protest: Jim a professional, Chetwind's registered letter with $100 (two $50s). Dick takes it; Parker's football captaincy meeting; Taylor and Sherman postpone election (Danby unanimous). Parker threatens Dick.
6. Ch VI: Chetwind (real-estate broker, country club) confirms; won't name agent. Jim denies, recalls second registered letter; Brady mentions Carpenter. Receipt signed by Jim.
7. Ch VII: Parker publicly accuses Jim; Steve Carter defends Dick and reveals Parker's knowledge; Carter says he'll nominate Jim for captain.
8. Ch VIII: Parker forces Carpenter to take letter; Shesgren refuses, is tied up in chair with trunk strap; Parker takes money ($100), marks bills; leaves letter in Jim's room.
9. Ch IX: Brady and Jim find slit envelope, empty, with blank folded note paper, under carpet (Friday morning). Post-office inspector visits. Chetwind names Shesgren as agent (Shesgren described by Jim: small, light, glasses, blue eyes, thin voice).
10. Ch X: Shesgren released, confesses; Dick's knife test: nick matches slit envelopes. Parker confesses and withdraws; Carpenter confesses; Jim forgives Carpenter.
11. Ch XI: Team to Cambridge; Boston trip. Jim kidnapped from taxicab by two men (one masked), taken to seashore. Jim recognizes possibly Parker's voice.
12. Ch XII: Harvard game (first of series, at Cambridge; Dick and Brady search). Jim escapes in a biplane, lands in Harvard field. Yale wins 1–0: Carter's stolen bases scored run; Brady long fly. Jim's wild pitch play with cap—Farquar tagged out at plate; double play by Jim on Bowen's steal; Yale won.
13. Ch XIII: Parker withdraws football captaincy; Jackson chosen. Foote and Parker plot: Foote suggests cribbing charge against Gray/Taylor.
14. Ch XIV: Dick warns Parker; Parker's "apology" plan. Mentions Jim kidnapped.
15. Ch XV: Parker steals Dick's confession sheet (blue paper) from his desk, substitutes blank blue sheet; Jack Tempest sees, Parker whistles "Marching Through Georgia." Foote tears up the confession.
16. Ch XVI: Examination papers—Sam gives Dick papers (cribbing notes in Taylor's and Gray's names). Dean suspends Gray and Taylor.
17. Ch XVII: Taylor shows Dick papers are fakes (wrong handwriting); dean gets anonymous letter; Dean says let them think they succeeded. Foote's instructor Gordon reports to dean. Foote breaks into Dwight Hall (night before commencement).
18. Ch XVIII: Commencement (June); Gray barred by faculty for blank exam book; Winston pitches; Harvard wins 4-? (Harvard one run ahead); Gray arrives in ninth, strikes out three.
19. Ch XIX: Dick finds fingerprints on book cover (Canfield had not washed hands); Foote's prints; Dick plans to trap.
20. Ch XX: Foote's plan: Jim will be kept from train. Parker tries to retrieve leaves from Canfield's catalogue—gone.
21. Ch XXI: Foote lures Jim (with Watson) into empty freight car; ventriloquist baby cry; Jim locked in car.
22. Ch XXII: Parker found by Brady at freight yard; Foote confesses; Foote's bread-print fingerprint matched; car number 34,576 Big Four Road, found at Kingston NY, West Shore RR. Jim rescued at 4 a.m. NY; Turkish bath.
23. Ch XXIII: Final game at Polo Grounds (Yale vs Harvard): Yale wins 3–2 in ninth; Jim pitches with bad arm, throws to 3rd for triple play with left hand. Sherman bunt/double; Jackson Texas Leaguer. Jim elected captain.
24. Ch XXIV: New London, Gale's Ferry; crew performing poorly (freshmen beat varsity; 10:59 vs 10:33). Hargreaves and Benton.
25. Ch XXV: Marina schooner (Gloucester-registered, fishing style). Svenson, Dennison, Barrows conspire to bet on Harvard, make Yale odds long; Harding sent Barrows.
26. Ch XXVI: Harvard also slows (Neilson). Thompson (Harvard coach) times Yale; Dick returns Murchison; Dick and Neilson exchange.
27. Ch XXVII: Betting; Brady's hammer joke; Tempest intercollegiate sprint champion; Watson predicts loss.
28. Ch XXVIII: Dick, Jim, Brady, Benton, Hargreaves night launch (Elihu Yale) past Marina; Harding's voice; Jim's owl/cat signal.
29. Ch XXIX: Jim fights Harding on road; Brady arrests threat; Harding sent to NY.
30. Ch XXX: Boat inspection; Jim sneaks aboard Marina at night; overhears wireless message (Bascom) "Barrows says O.K."; caught by searchlight, held by Barrows/Svenson; Jim escapes into hold.
31. Ch XXXI: Jim finds magnet coil and hollow keel model (iron groove); map with three blue crosses; hides.
32. Ch XXXII: Jim escapes by scuttling Marina from inside; swims out; Dick, Neilson, search warrant; Marina sinks; magnets in shells; crews rigged with old shells.
33. Ch XXXIII: Race day; Barrows's crew betting; Svenson furious, Barnes.
34. Ch XXXIV: Yale wins: four-oared (by less than 2 seconds), freshmen (ten lengths), varsity by less than 2 seconds. Jim in hydroplane stops miniature clockwork torpedo.
35. Ch XXXV: Boston wants revenge; Dick proposes Yale players vs Boston game (Briggs/Bowen); Olympics talk (Stockholm); Dick's lumber venture in Maine; team: Brady/Jim battery, Carter 3B, Jackson 2B, Green SS, Maxwell, Brayson, Tuthill OF, Dick at 1B.
36. Ch XXXVI: Foote's gambling debts, Marsten's gambling house; Barrows recruits Foote.
37. Ch XXXVII: Barrows plans bank robbery with Marsten; Riggs owes $1,000 (lost betting).
38. Ch XXXVIII: Riggs embezzles $1,000 (Marsten's tip); Barrows, posing socialist, recruits Riggs.
39. Ch XXXIX: Dick deposits $5,000 at Elm National; Barrows gets serial numbers; Phelps (financier) pays Barrows $5,000 to ruin Dick.
40. Ch XL: Marsten's house (secret ring code); Bascom works on vault combinations.
41. Ch XLI: Night of the robbery: Jim rescues watchman, knocked out by Bascom with slingshot; Barrows and Bascom escape with $2,500 each; watchman gagged in cellar.
42. Ch XLII: Jim found in vault (morning); bank accuses him; Bromlow; Brady's father's telegram gives authority.
43. Ch XLIII: Riggs's counterfeit bills; Foote carried money to Riggs; Jim arrested, released on bail; watchman identifies him.
44. Ch XLIV: Barrows arrested in NYC; 5 years; Riggs suspended sentence; Jim cleared.
45. Ch XLV: Fourth of July game vs Boston (Briggs). Jim's arm bad early; 8–7 Yale win; Dick captains; bunt tactics; Jim's out/touched; Jackson, Green, Brady's triple.

(Gray, Taylor, Shesgren, Carpenter reconciled; Parker reformed, cheers Jim at end.)

# BOOK 2 NOTES: "Elsie's Motherhood" (Martha Finley; 1876; Gutenberg #14566; sequel to Elsie's Womanhood)

## Characters
- **Elsie Travilla** (née Dinsmore), wife of **Edward (Mr.) Travilla**, mother. Children: **Elsie** (9, "little Elsie"), **Edward "Eddie"**, **Violet "Vi"** (5), **Harold** (about 3), **Herbert** (baby). Nurses: **Dinah**, **Aunt Chloe** (mammy/nurse), **Aunt Dicey** (housekeeper), **Uncle Joe** (old man, carries mail), **Solon** (coachman), **Ben** (Travilla's body servant, foster-brother), **Prilla**, **Minna**, **Tom**, **Aunt Sally** (nurse of quarter), **Jack** (servant), Bruno (Newfoundland), Beppo (bay horse), Prince and Princess (ponies, Eddie's and Elsie's).
- **Horace Dinsmore** (Elsie's father; "papa"), **Rose** (Rosie) Dinsmore (his wife's? no—Horace's wife Rose, Elsie's stepmother/aunt-like; Rose is Elsie's sister? — Rose is Elsie's sister by marriage; Rosie Dinsmore = Elsie's half-sister/daughter of Horace and Rose). **Horace Dinsmore Jr.** (Elsie's brother). Grandfather **Horace Dinsmore Sr.**? (text: "old Mr. Dinsmore" = Elsie's grandfather, father of Horace Sr.? Treat as "grandpa Dinsmore" at Roselands).
- Roselands family (Dinsmore cousins): aunts **Louise Conly** (widow) and **Enna Johnson** (widow); their children **Calhoun "Cal" Conly** (~21), **Arthur Conly** (son), **Virginia** and **Isadore Conly**, **Walter (Wal) Conly**, **Molly Percival**, **Dick Percival**, **Bob** and **Betty** (small, Enna's?). Mrs. Conly's daughter Virginia; Enna's son Dick Percival is Molly's brother.
- Ashlands: **Sophie Carrington** (widow of Harold? "Sophie's husband died"), her children **Herbert Carrington, Meta Carrington** (~9), **Daisy** (ill), **Harry Carrington**; **Mrs. Carrington** (elder, Sophie's mother-in-law, aged), nephew **George Boyd** (Ku Klux).
- Fairview: **Mr. Robert Leland** (northern, Union officer, carpet-bagger), **Mrs. Mary Leland**, children **Archie**, **Mary**; the **Fosters** (Mrs. Foster; daughters **Annie**, **Lucinda**; son **Wilkins Foster** who dies after Mrs. Leland's son Archie/she shot him).
- Pinegrove, Springbrook (Mr. Wood, pastor; Mrs. Wood), Lucy Ross (Phil, Gertrude Ross—children of Lucy Ross, staying at Ashlands), Miss Fisk (governess).
- Mr. Lilburn ("Cousin Ronald", Scottish ventriloquist, relative of Elsie's maternal grandmother, Elsie Grayson), Aunt Wealthy (Lansdale), May and Harry (Lansdale).
- Daly family: Mr. Daly (minister), Mrs. Daly, son Frank (Harold's friend).
- Villains: Dr. Savage (drunk), Jim White, Green (of Ku Klux), Snell/Martin (detective), Jones (victim stage driver), Blake, Bill Dobbs, Tom Arnold, Smith.

## Key events in order
1. Anniversary (10 years married) at Ion; children; invitation; Elsie wears wedding dress (veil, orange blossoms); ceremony repeated by Mr. Wood.
2. Ashlands/Roselands visits; Phil Ross disobeys Miss Fisk; Enna dislikes Elsie; Louise and Enna stay at Roselands with Father.
3. Eddie and Vi's pony rides; charity: Vi and Elsie buy red flannel for Aunt Delia; Eddie buys tobacco for Uncle Jack.
4. Ku Klux outrages; Leland, Dinsmore, Travilla discussed; Foster, Boyd, Conly argue politics (Foster calls them scalawags).
5. Calhoun Conly joins Klan under Boyd/Foster; mother Louise and Enna sew disguises (cotton, linen, red braid); Dick and Walter find disguises in closet.
6. Ku Klux night: Vi wanders out in sleep, witnesses murder of stage driver Jones; Bruno finds her; Travilla carries her home.
7. Eddie accidentally shoots Travilla (Dick/Walter tease and dare; Eddie disobeys father's order). Travilla wounded (scalp, fall), recovers. Eddie repentant; forgiven.
8. Christmas/Dec: Ku Klux raids; Dinsmores and Travillas resist; Leland arrives; Boyd arrested for hand-print on night dress.
9. Cal sees threat; Dick and Walter dressed in disguises frighten children; Travilla whips Dick; Cal whips Walter.
10. Birthday of Dick and Walter; ponies sent; forgiveness; Calhoun's conversion talk with Elsie ("believe and be saved").
11. Fall 1868: Ku Klux raids on Ion's quarter; school-house burned; Mr. Lilburn ventriloquist scares Klan (breakfast chicken, statue, Bruno talks); soap-and-lye defense at Ion; Klan repulsed; Lilburn bugle trick.
12. Leland shot in leg; hides at Ion; Uncle Mose dies (Travilla and Elsie present); funeral; Aunt Dicey's soap.
13. Foster dies (~age 30) after Leland's wife shot him; Elsie aids Foster girls teaching; Leland reconciled.
14. Lilburn arrives (Scottish cousin); Calhoun reconsidered; Viamede visit planned: all families go to Viamede (Louisiana plantation) for winter.
15. Journey by steamer; gambler Nick Ward cheated; Lilburn ventriloquism exposes; Mr. Daly; tobacco lecture.
16. Viamede: play-room with grandmother's (Elsie Grayson's) toys; Meta steals key, breaks plate; Vi confesses; Meta pries and is caught by Lilburn/Mrs. Carrington; Meta banned from picnic.
17. Picnic: Herbert crosses broken bridge, falls in stream, rescued by Bruno and Mr. Daly; Eddie asks about cowardice vs. duty.

## Chronology notes
- Story ends (Chapter 28): children reflect on Viamede; Elsie's closing quote.
